thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 [HIGH] decode/stream node gpu-3 reporting repeated CUDA_OOM during streaming decode. auto-pager created. Affected routes: /v1/stream (region: eu-west-1).
oncall-ml: saw this spike ~2m ago, we're seeing continuous OOMs on gpu-3 and gpu-7, same hostpool. Requests are getting dropped, some customer sessions aborted.
sre-tilly: oncall acked. tagging eng-runtime & ops. Initial triage: OOMs correlate with long-lived streaming sessions that keep KV caches open; memory graph shows sustained growth not reclaimed.
eng-runtime: noted a canary deploy 25m ago that changed header parsing in stream proxy (x-request-max -> interpreted as absolute token cap by the new decoder path). Rolling back now.
ops-tom: pulling node out of rotation (gpu-3) and draining sessions. Command: ```./nodectl cordon gpu-3 && ./nodectl drain gpu-3 --force --evict-sessions```
support-jess: support queue seeing ~40 customer errors (stream aborted). Collecting affected customer IDs. Most report truncated outputs and HTTP 502.
cs-lead: notifying impacted customers with a short note: investigating, mitigation in progress, ETA 30m.
oncall-ml: quick capture of an offending trace here (stack + headers): ```[STREAM TRACE] client=acme-inc header:X-Request-Max: 10000 route:/v1/stream mode:chunked decode_path:new-decoder-v2 memory:gpu-usage=14.2GB->24.8GB->OOM```
eng-runtime: confirmed new-decoder-v2 treats X-Request-Max as absolute token limit instead of a hint; defaulting to 10k when present. SDKs/clients sometimes send huge values or unset caps which got interpreted as huge max length -> runaway generation. This is different from our usual max_tokens enforcement.
sre-tilly: mitigation plan: 1) immediate rollback of the canary so decoder uses legacy header semantics (eng-runtime rolling), 2) hotfix on proxy to enforce per-route hard cap (2000 tokens) until patch lands, 3) evict/terminate stuck sessions on affected nodes to reclaim memory.
eng-runtime: rollback in progress - canary stopped, traffic shift to stable in flight. Patch PR opened to coerce X-Request-Max into a request-scoped ceiling and log violations.
ops-tom: drained gpu-3 and gpu-7, forced eviction done, nodes restarting. Observed memory reclaimed on restart.
incident-bot: deploybot: rollback stable->new-decoder-v2 halted at 4444203450 by eng-runtime.
sre-tilly: after node restarts memory looks stable. however we still see elevated error rates from clients that hit truncated responses during the incident window. need to identify in-flight sessions that retried.
support-jess: collated customer IDs: [acme-inc, beta-studios, fintech-solutions]. Opening high-priority tickets and attaching logs.
eng-runtime: hot-proxy rule applied: ```headers.enforce('X-Request-Max', max=2000)``` on /v1/stream for all regions. Will monitor for false positives.
oncall-ml: telemetry check: token generation rate back to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback. No further OOMs on gpu-3/gpu-7.
cs-lead: customer note draft: "We've identified and rolled back a canary change that caused an incorrect interpretation of an optional header which could increase generation length. We've applied an emergency cap and restarted affected nodes. We're following up with a permanent fix and will issue post-incident summary." Approve?
sre-tilly: approve. Add timeline and affected request counts to postmortem.
eng-runtime: follow-up actions: 1) patch proxy and new-decoder-v2 to default to client-hint semantics (treat X-Request-Max as advisory, not absolute), 2) add early token-budget guard in decoder to stop runaway before large KV growth, 3) add test asserting header->limit mapping behavior, 4) instrument per-session KV size metrics for faster detection.
ops-tom: will build a k8s pod-eviction runbook for streaming node memory leaks and add an automated quarantine label if OOM rate > 5/min.
support-jess: will send interim customer updates and attach remediation ETA.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, impact=partial (some requests dropped, no data loss), next_handoff=4444204600.
oncall-ml: handing off to next oncall, please review logs for any late-failing sessions and verify patch rollout.
sre-tilly: oncall handoff done. If new OOMs appear escalate to eng-runtime immediately and run evacuation script.
eng-runtime: creating postmortem doc and PR references. Will coordinate root-cause writeup and include timeline + comms.
cs-lead: customer communication sent. Will follow up with prioritized affected-customer callbacks.
support-jess: closing incident thread in support after tickets created.
ops-tom: nodes healthy in eu-west-1, continuing 15m monitoring.
incident-bot: final note: ran containment steps, rollback completed, emergency cap applied, cleanup tasks assigned. Postmortem owner: eng-runtime.
